newsitem.title: USA: AMR sees two pct annual capacity growth.
newsitem.headline: AMR sees two pct annual capacity growth.

text.p: AMR Corp Chairman Robert Crandall said on Thursday that he expects American Airline's capacity to grow about two percent annually over the next four to five years.
"Total capacity growth for next four or five years ought to be about two percent -- a little less in domestic markets, a little more in international," Crandall said.
"Two percent annual growth is entirely consistent with rate at which the market will grow. It will allow us to remain competitive and remain profitable as well," he said.
"We think restraining capacity is important to sustaining the profitability of the U.S. airline business," Crandall said at a press conference at Dallas/Forth Worth International Airport.
"We do not want to grow very rapidly, but we do want the ability to grow in those markets where we do best," he said.

AMR earlier on Thursday announced firm orders for 103 Boeing Co aircraft and said it has purchase rights for an additional 527 jets. The deal makes Boeing American's exclusive jet supplier through 2018.

The jet order will allow AMR to grow capacity as it streamlines its fleet. Having common aircraft models in its fleet will allow the carrier to trim training, maintenance and operating costs, AMR said.
The aircraft deal will have a "favorable impact on our cost structure over the long-term," Crandall said.
